_source: Hand-transcribed from the City of Kannapolis Stormwater page and its current fee schedule (Table 8.1). Flood zones are FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer, read by etl/build_stormwater.py into data/generated/geo/floodzones.json; FRIS (the NC Flood Risk Information System) is the State's official address lookup.
name: Stormwater & Flooding
what: Stormwater is rain that runs off roofs, roads, driveways and parking lots. It picks up oil, grease, pet waste, lawn chemicals and grass clippings on the way.
two_systems: Storm drains and sewers are separate systems in Kannapolis. Sinks, showers and toilets go to a treatment plant; storm drains carry rain, and anything else poured into them, straight to the nearest creek or lake without treatment.

report.title: Stormwater problems
report.text: Clogged or broken storm drains, flooding from the drainage system

report.title: Illegal discharges
report.text: Anything other than rain going into a storm drain: oil, paint, chemicals, soapy wash water, sewage

report.title: STOP MUD
report.text: Mud or sediment washing off a construction site or eroding land

tips.text: Never pour oil, gasoline, paint or chemicals into a storm drain
Keep leaves, yard debris and trash out of the storm drain near you
Pick up pet waste and put it in the trash
Use pesticides, weed killers and fertilizer sparingly, and follow the directions
Fix car leaks; wash your car on the lawn or at a car wash that recycles water
Sweep driveways and sidewalks instead of hosing them down
A rain barrel on a downspout holds back runoff and waters your garden
Point downspouts and driveway runoff toward lawns and gardens
Keep a septic tank, if you have one, pumped and maintained

permit.intro: The City's federal Phase II stormwater permit (NCS000413) requires a stormwater program with six parts:

fee.intro: The federal government doesn't pay for local stormwater programs, so the City charges a monthly stormwater fee on every water and sewer bill. It's based on impervious area (roofs, driveways, patios and other hard surfaces rain can't soak into).

explain.name: Floodway
explain.text: The creek channel and the land right beside it that must stay open to carry floodwater. Building here is tightly restricted.

explain.name: 100-year floodplain
explain.text: A 1% chance of flooding in any year, about a 1-in-4 chance over a 30-year mortgage. Lenders require flood insurance here.

explain.name: 500-year floodplain
explain.text: A 0.2% chance in any year: lower risk, but floods do reach it. Insurance is optional and usually cheaper.

flood.insurance: Homeowners insurance doesn't cover flooding. Flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program or a private insurer usually takes 30 days to start.
